intent: Enforce atomic built-in tool binding replacement and disable across supported production mutation and restore paths, retain profile/tool ownership and rollback, and replace the impossible nullable-index instrumentation assumption with behavior regressions. Preserve authentic Room53 and mandatory acceptance receipts.
findings: Without the database callback, Room53 table/index definitions allow repeated built-in rows with identical profile/tool and NULL connection. Incoming85389f14 supplies the INSERT/UPDATE guard.

Repository UI bindings already use deterministic IDs, so ordinary concurrent enables alone do not create duplicates. Its separate delete/insert still loses an existing grant if insertion fails and is not atomic with disable or config/legacy imports carrying arbitrary saved IDs.

Configuration and legacy import already call insertBinding; its central transaction now collapses only the exact NULL-connection profile/tool scope while preserving legacy names and rejecting binding-ID ownership changes before mutation.

Incoming complete backup staging normalizes historical duplicates by newest timestamp and descending binding ID inside its caller transaction, before guarded destination copying. The redundant local post-copy normalizer was removed. Room schema53 exports remain unchanged.
